moTa: From the 1st to the 8th of the twelfth lunar month, An Nhiên Pagoda marks the day the Buddha attained enlightenment under the Bodhi tree. Meditation mats are laid out in the yard, and the pagoda kitchen cooks milk porridge as a gentle symbol of the Middle Way: neither too harsh nor too lax. It's a season to sit still, see your heart clearly, be patient with yourself, and look back on the year.

loiChao.noiDung: The twelfth lunar month is here. Come in and sit quietly under the Bodhi tree.
An Nhiên Pagoda wishes you a quiet, clear-hearted Bodhi Day season.
The year-end wind is chilly. Come into the main hall, sit and breathe slowly.
Hello. There's no hurry today. Let's just sit still together.
The kitchen has just made a hot pot of milk porridge. Come have a small bowl.
The Bodhi tree in the yard is still green in the winter cold. Come and see it.
This Bodhi Day season, may you see your heart a little more clearly each day.
Hello, twelfth month. The old year is closing; let's look back on it gently.
The morning star shone over the pagoda roof. Wishing you a calm, clear day.
Put your phone down for one minute and listen to the pagoda bell ring out.
The 8th of the twelfth month is near. Thank you for visiting so patiently.
The meditation mat is ready. Sit as long as feels right; no need to strain.

thongDiep.noiDung: The Buddha sat still for a long time before seeing clearly. Clarity often comes to those patient enough to stay with themselves.
The bowl of milk porridge in the old story reminds us that caring for the body is also part of the path.
Not too strict, not too loose. The middle road is often the one you can walk the longest.
Sitting still for five minutes is not wasted time. It's when you give time back to yourself.
Only when the mind is as calm as a windless lake can you see the bottom. Don't stir the water looking for answers.
At year's end, try writing down three things you did well. Looking back isn't only for finding faults.
Thoughts come and go like clouds over a mountain. You don't need to chase them or push them away.
Eat a bowl of porridge slowly. Feel the warmth spread through your hands; that is a simple mindfulness practice.
Enlightenment doesn't drop out of the sky. It comes from many days of quietly observing and not giving up.
If your mind feels tangled today, don't blame yourself. Noticing the tangle is already the start of waking up.
A year leaves many things unfinished. Pick one small task to complete and save the rest for the new year.
Patience isn't sitting and waiting. It's continuing to do what's right before you see results.
The Bodhi tree grows bit by bit through many seasons of rain and sun. Inner growth can't be rushed either.
Before replying to an upsetting message, take three breaths. Three breaths can change a whole conversation.
Seeing your heart clearly means seeing both the beautiful and the not-yet-beautiful, without rushing to judge.
Some questions don't need answers right away. Let them sit beside you for a while; the answers will come on their own.
Everyone is busy in the last month of the year. Amid the rush, one minute of stillness is a gift to yourself.
The morning star rises whether or not anyone watches. The good you do matters even when no one sees it.
A tired body makes a restless mind. Go to bed a little earlier tonight; that, too, is a way to care for your mindfulness.
Don't compare yourself this year with others. Compare yourself with last year's you, and honor each small step.
Meditation doesn't need a perfect posture. A reasonably straight back and relaxed shoulders are enough to begin.
When you feel sad, try naming that feeling softly. Once it's named, it often eases.
A plain bowl of porridge offered with care can lift someone more than any expensive gift.
At year's end, forgive one old hurt. With less baggage, you'll step into the new year lighter.
Stillness isn't far away. It lives right in the pause between two of your breaths.
Everyone sometimes wants to give up. In those moments, remember how far you've already come.
Tidy a corner of your desk, tidy a corner of your heart. Order on the outside can sometimes bring clarity within.
Understanding yourself is the first step to caring for yourself. Once you care for yourself, you'll have the strength to care for others.
Your inner light doesn't need anyone to kindle it for you. It only waits for you to pause long enough to notice.
When the 8th passes, the meditation mats will be rolled up. Keep the habit of sitting still a few minutes each day.

loiNguyen.noiDung: I vow to spend a few quiet minutes each evening looking back on the day.
I vow to be more patient with myself when things aren't working out yet.
May everyone worn out at year's end get a good night's sleep.
I vow to look back on this year with gratitude instead of regret.
May anyone feeling overwhelmed find a quiet space to breathe.
I vow to eat and drink in moderation, neither too strict with myself nor overindulgent.
May my parents stay healthy through the cold winter days.
I vow to pause and take three breaths before speaking in anger.
May those working far from home soon be reunited with their families.
I vow to finish one unfinished task before the old year closes.
May everyone have someone to offer them a bowl of hot porridge when they need it.
I vow to notice my feelings and name them gently.
May everyone studying for exams stay calm enough to do their best.
I vow to forgive one old hurt so my heart can feel lighter.
May young children grow up surrounded by patient grown-ups.
I vow to scroll less before bed so my mind can rest.
Thank you to the year gone by, for the happy days and the hard ones.
I vow to learn to sit with sadness instead of running from it.
May those who are ill find more strength to get through this winter.
I vow to slow down during the busy last weeks of the lunar year.
May every family have an evening to sit together and talk.
I vow to write down three good things each day until the year ends.
May those who feel lonely have a friend drop by to check on them.
I vow not to rush to judge others before I fully understand.
May all beings stay warm and find shelter through the cold season.
I vow to keep up one good habit even when progress is slow.
May the world find more moments of quiet amid all the noise.
I vow to care for my body like a lamp I want to keep burning bright.
May everyone searching for their way see their next step clearly.
I vow to enter the new year with a clear and gentle heart.

tho: I sit in stillness where the Bodhi grows
And hear my breathing as it comes and goes
So many ripples drifting on the tide
Grow still, and then I find my heart is wide
queDacBiet.loiGiai: Sitting still doesn't mean the heart has no waves. Thoughts still come and drift like small ripples on water. This verse suggests not rushing to clear them away; just stay seated and let them settle. When the surface is smooth, you'll find your heart is wider than you thought. The Bodhi Day season is a time to practice that patience, one breath at a time.
queDacBiet.loiKhuyen: Tonight, sit still for three minutes before bed. You don't need to think about anything special; just count your breaths from one to ten, then begin again.

tho: A winter bowl of porridge, warm and plain
Sweet as my mother's lullaby refrain
The road is long, the mist hangs thick and gray;
Walk at your pace, and you will find the way
queDacBiet.loiGiai: The story of the bowl of milk porridge before the night of enlightenment reminds us that the path doesn't ask us to punish ourselves. This verse is about keeping a pace you can sustain. On a long road, take it step by step, rest at times, and enjoy a warm meal. Those who care for themselves can travel far. What you're working toward will come through steadiness, not by pushing yourself to exhaustion.
queDacBiet.loiKhuyen: Today, eat a warm meal slowly and ask yourself: am I pushing myself too hard at anything right now?

tho: At year's end on the porch I sit a while
And look back on the days gone by and smile
The morning star climbs bright into the sky
And next year I'll walk steadier, head high
queDacBiet.loiGiai: The end of the year is a good time to sit down and look at the days gone by without blame. Some things worked out, some didn't yet, and all of them are lessons. This verse is like the morning star: the sky is still dark, but morning is on its way. When you look back clearly, you'll know how to step more steadily next year.
queDacBiet.loiKhuyen: Write down one thing you're proud of this year and one thing you'd like to do differently. Put the note somewhere you'll see it.
